questions.q: Green Arrow debuted in 1941's More Fun Comics #73, the same issue that introduced which other hero?
questions.why: More Fun Comics #73 (cover date November 1941) introduced both Green Arrow and Aquaman.

questions.q: Which writer created Green Arrow, with the character designed by artist George Papp?
questions.why: Mort Weisinger created him, drawing on Robin Hood and a movie serial called The Green Archer, and George Papp designed his look.

questions.q: Who is Green Arrow's original teenage sidekick?
questions.why: Speedy, Roy Harper, debuted alongside Green Arrow in 1941 and mirrors Batman's Robin.

questions.q: In the comics, wealthy businessman Oliver Queen is a celebrity in which fictional metropolis?
questions.why: Oliver Queen owns Queen Industries and is a well-known figure in Star City, which he uses to hide his Green Arrow identity.

questions.q: Which legendary outlaw archer partly inspired Green Arrow?
questions.why: Besides an outlaw-archer theme, the hero's creator borrowed ideas from Batman.

questions.q: In Mike Grell's 1987 revamp of Green Arrow, to which city did the hero relocate?
questions.why: Under Mike Grell, Green Arrow dropped trick arrows and moved from Star City to Seattle, Washington.

questions.q: Which artist gave Green Arrow his Van Dyke beard and redesigned costume in 1969?
questions.why: Neal Adams redesigned him in The Brave and the Bold #85, and Denny O'Neil then rebuilt his personality as a champion for the poor.

questions.q: In 1970, an acclaimed socially conscious series paired Green Arrow with which fellow hero?
questions.why: The early 1970s stories by Denny O'Neil and Neal Adams paired the left-leaning archer with the law-and-order Green Lantern.

questions.q: Alongside Count Vertigo, which master archer is called Green Arrow's archenemy?
questions.why: Merlyn, a master archer, and Count Vertigo, who disrupts balance and perception, are named as his archenemies.

questions.q: Who starred as Oliver Queen in the CW series Arrow, which debuted in 2012?
questions.why: Stephen Amell played Oliver Queen on Arrow, starting the Arrowverse; Justin Hartley had played him on Smallville.
